subject: machining
intro: Machining leads to precision manufacturing: machinists who cut metal to thousandths, inspectors who judge parts against tolerances, and technicians who build and test the prototypes engineering teams design.

roles.title: Machinists
roles.what: Set up and operate machine tools to produce precision metal parts and instruments, fabricating, modifying or repairing mechanical instruments using knowledge of mechanics, mathematics, metal properties, layout and machining procedures.
roles.where: Units three and four are the job itself — lathe setup, workholding, turning and threading, speeds and feeds, then milling machines, work holding, indexing and contouring — on the precision measurement foundation of unit one.

roles.title: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
roles.what: Inspect, test and sort the output of production lines: measure finished parts against specifications and tolerances, record results, reject nonconforming work, and help trace quality problems back to their source.
roles.where: The quality and inspection unit — tolerance systems and GD and T basics, surface finish, precision measurement instruments — teaches exactly the dimensional checking this role performs all day.

roles.title: Mechanical Engineering Technologists and Technicians
roles.what: Assist mechanical engineers in designing, developing and testing machines and equipment: build and modify prototypes and test apparatus, run experiments, collect and analyse data, and help turn drawings into working hardware.
roles.where: Shop-floor skill in turning, milling and CNC setup lets you machine the prototypes engineers specify, and the materials and machinability unit explains how stock choices shape designs and tests.
